comment_text.value:
> So what is this conflict all about? Is there bigger geopolitical price tag attached to victory in Iran? Or US is just besieged by corruption to the extent campaign finding from Israel lobby as they say dictated much of the foreign policy than national interest?

An optimist would say:

America doesn't like Iran because it's a theocratic dictatorship that funds terrorist groups throughout the region, supplies drones to Russia, fires missiles at the only democracy in the region (Israel) and is pursuing nuclear weapons.

As energy markets are global, middle east politics impacts America's vital national interests, and prices consumers pay at the pump, even if America is a net exporter of oil.

Iran had a series of nationwide protests https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Iranian_prot... indicating there was widespread popular support for a new, less theocratic government.

Trump thought they could go in with a surgical strike, knock out the theocratic leaders and the nuclear facilities, enabling the protesters to overthrow the remains of the government, while the army steps back like we saw in the 2011 Egyptian revolution. Then they'd turn into a peace-loving democracy, and Trump would go down in history as having defeated one of America's long-term antagonists, making him a winner and a tough guy, and really showing Obama how it's done.

A cynic would say:

Trump wanted a distraction from the Epstein files (which this war has 100% delivered) and/or a country that wanted this war to happen has the Epstein evidence to blackmail him with.

Having deliberately installed loyal incompetents in leadership positions, even though military planners were 100% aware the Strait of Hormuz would get closed, and that their drones are an order of magnitude cheaper than our drone interceptors, that knowledge was dismissed by the executive.

Being able to make oil prices rise and fall by tweeting is an easy way to make money if you're exempt from the justice system.

Having the war drag on might not be good for Republican performance in the midterm elections - but Trump can't run for a third term, so he doesn't much care if the party is left in a shambles.

comment_text.value:
Both the reasons (AIPAC + pricing Oil in USD helps finance our deficits) are why we were there. But both of those reasons have been severely weakened, to the point of probably being eliminated anyways:

1. After the midterms, we'll get a read on how much AIPAC is still able to buy congressmen.

2. Before Trump obeyed Israel and bombed Iran, we had the illusion of being invincible. But now, we are faced with the brut reality that we cannot guarantee the flow of oil through the Hormuz straight, nor almost anywhere else in that whole hemisphere. Even to Europe: Ask Putin how much drones have changed the game.

This really eliminates any remaining motivations to keep pricing oil in USD. Which removes most of the motivations for the world to keep financing our deficit.

At this point our best option is to just leave the region, and try to transition to renewables absolutely as fast as we can. Oh, and raise taxes on everybody, because demand for our bonds is going to crater.

comment_text.value:
> This seems contradictory. The first seems like wishful thinking/unclear rationalization. The second implies a contradiction. Why are the polls relevant unless you mean to suggest this war involved more commitment? Yet it also ended in failure?

I'm saying that America was not really all that motivated for Afghanistan (aside from the start), Iraq, Vietnam, or any major conflict since Korea. We can lose and life goes on. The stock market stays up, businesses keep doing business, the government stays in power, the conflict isn't existential in even the most minor sense except for that tiny minority that's directly involved. And those conflicts were largely insurgencies and attempts at nation-building.

A kinetic war at sea with a nation state like China is what America was built to fight, although perhaps less so now that the Trump admin has wasted most of our advanced munitions on Iran. They have a navy for us to sink and fighters and bombers to shoot down, and if we do that well enough we win! There's no caves to hide in, no religious insurgencies to plant IEDs, no land to occupy, no nation-building.

I'm not saying we wouldn't have casualties, but I think in a conventional war we'd do better against China than Iran.

> Anyway we'll have to agree to disagree on most of the rest. I don't know what metric your using to define "MAGA" but I don't think I share it. 80 million people roughly voted for the Jan 6th guy. His coalition is (or at least was) pretty wide. He will probably lose the midterms like most presidents. It's not clear he really cares or that it will really matter.

Most of those 80 million were not hardcore MAGA, just uninformed and pissed at Biden for whatever reason. Plenty of them have fallen off the train in the last year and a half. Between DOGE, ICE, Epstein, Iran and stepping the corruption into overdrive, there's at least one major thing that will keep many of them from voting for him again. Even the MAGA base started to turn on him after the MOU with Iran came out, he had to backtrack on that quickly

But yeah, good talk!

> We don't commit precisely because we are so dominant there is no need.

> Just look at public opinion at the start of Afghanistan. It's a shame Bush and Obama bungled it so badly.

This seems contradictory. The first seems like wishful thinking/unclear rationalization. The second implies a contradiction. Why are the polls relevant unless you mean to suggest this war involved more commitment? Yet it also ended in failure?

What was the last war America won against an adversary like today's China? Who is signing up for such a war today? If all these other wars have been a "war of choice" why would war with China be any different? His coalition is (or at least was) pretty wide. He will probably lose the midterms like most presidents. It's not clear he really cares or that it will really matter.

Anyway, I hope you are right and I appreciate the back and forth. Thanks!
